conflicts.description: Both wiring drawings count four lamps on flash group 8R: the operator manual's coil-driver drawing (printed page 33) prints '(2) LOW LEFT PLFD (2) INSERT (4) 89' and the schematic book's wiring sheet (printed page 50) '(2) PLFD (2) INSERT (4) NO.89'. The operator manual's Flash Lamp / Coil Tests location drawing (printed page 32) prints one 8R callout on the playfield and its Backbox Flash Lamps drawing two 8R sockets, three in all. The 1.12 ROM names the drive '2-INS 1-TAR PIT' and the retained table comments it 'Flash Playfield Low Left + Backbox Insert(x2)', but a name and a comment describe the group without counting its bulbs. The record keeps three as the working quantity. Resolution path: on a production machine, select 8R in the Select Coil test and count the lamps that light on the lower left of the playfield and in the backbox insert, or count the 8R sockets on its harness; an owner of the machine could do it.

The operator manual prints lamp 31 'Captive Ball X2' and lamp 32 'Ticket' in its Lamp Matrix Chart and description list, and its Lamp Locations drawing (printed pages 30-31) prints 31 at both captive-ball inserts and 32 alone in the open centre of the playfield; the schematic book's Playfield Lamp Wiring Diagram (printed page 53) names 31 'Left Captive Ball' and 32 'Right Captive Ball'. The 1.12 ROM names 31 'CAPTIVE BALLS X2' and 32 'TICKET', drives 31 and never 32 while the captive-ball and return-lane switches close in a game, and the retained table fades both captive-ball inserts with 31; the record follows them, but none of them shows a production harness. Resolution path: run the single-lamp test on lamp 32 of a production machine, or trace the right captive-ball insert's socket wires to their lamp-matrix row and column, and see whether that insert lights on 32 or on 31; an owner of the machine could do it.

The operator manual's coil-driver drawing (printed page 33) returns the common of drive 9's four No. 89 lamps (two in the crane cab, two in the backbox insert) to power-supply connector CN3 pin 6, an unswitched +32 V. The schematic book's wiring sheet (printed page 50) draws the same four lamps on '+32 VDCR PPBJ6-4/5', the ORG supply of the right-set flash groups 25-32, which the Left/Right relay 10 switches on only while it is energised (printed page 32). On the first drawing 9 lights its lamps whatever 10's state; on the second only while 10 is on. The 1.12 ROM had 10 on at every one of the 51 times 9 turned on in the 7 retained runs, so the runs cannot tell the two apart, and PinMAME publishes 9 whatever 10's state. The record keeps the public binding at 9 and records neither supply nor a relay relationship. Resolution path: with the power off, check whether the common wire of the crane-cab or backbox-insert drive-9 sockets is continuous with PPB connector J6 pins 4-5 or with power-supply connector CN3 pin 6, or fire 9 in the Select Coil test with the relay released and see whether the lamps light; an owner of a production machine could do it.

The retained runs do not settle which public level is which position. With -6 at 1, the first Black press from attract entered the diagnostics and, in the printer-interface run, Black stepped backwards through the adjustments from 99 to 58; with -6 at 0, Black from attract walked towards the audits, yet the Lamp Test with -6 at 0 stepped from lamp 1 to 64, 63 and down, which the manual's text reads as REVERSE. s11.c hands the PIA the level uncomplemented (core_getSw(DE_SWUPDN)). It draws the contact open and prints 'CLOSE ??????' under the switch's label, so the page leaves open in which of the two positions the contact is closed. s11.c declares MDRV_DIPS(1), commented '(actually a jumper)', and pia2a_r reads it as core_getDip(0) << 7 on PIA2 PA7, annotated 'PA7 (I) Jumper W7'. The factory name is J8: the CPU Board Logic Diagram (schematic book printed page 56) draws PA7, pin 9 of the 6821 at 11B (the PIA whose port B the same page takes to CN3, which PinMAME publishes as PIA2's), pulled up to +5 through RA19-9 (4.7K) and taken to ground through a link labelled J8, drawn as two terminals joined by a dashed line. No retained page says what the ROM does with the bit or how the link is fitted at the factory, so its meaning stays unknown.

mechanisms.behavior: The 6 Ball Switch Assy. (500-5683-01) holds up to six balls on trough switches 9 (left, the drain end) to 14; the lockout coil on drive 1 (25-1240, the schematic's '6 Ball Ass'y Lockout') moves the ball at 14 into the release position 15 (Trough #7, typed 180-5118-00 against 180-5119-00 for 9-14), and the Ball Release on drive 2 (23-800) kicks it from 15 into the shooter lane, where switch 16 senses it. ROM evidence (1.12 game start, the host moving the balls): with balls on 9-14 and 15 empty, Start pulsed the lockout 3 times; once a ball reached 15 the ROM pulsed the release 6 times while 15 stayed closed. The host moved every ball, so the counts are the ROM's retries, not travel times. The schematic book's Trough Assembly page (printed page 75) draws the 6 Ball Switch Assembly 500-5683-01 with six subminiature switches (180-5119-00; its parts table prints 12) in a row under the sloped outhole bracket and one miniature switch (180-5118-00) on its switch bracket beside the top of the release coil (23-800), which stands vertically under the low end of the row with its plunger and spring; above it the page draws the Lock Ball Assembly 500-5684-01, its 25-1240 coil laid horizontally with the plunger, spring and link at one end and a lock-ball cam below the link. The page does not say which way either plunger moves. The retained table rests its balls on trough kickers sw9-sw14 that roll them towards sw14 (UpdateTroughTimer, script lines 1089-1101), and its SolTrough and SolRelease kick sw14 into sw15 and sw15 into the shooter lane (lines 1108-1121).
mechanisms.label: Six-Ball Trough, Lockout and Ball Release

mechanisms.behavior: The Ball Launch Assy (500-5477-01) on drive 3, 23-800 through the PPB booster Q5 and named 'COIL: AUTO LAUNCH 50V' by the ROM, launches the ball resting on the shooter lane switch 16. The cabinet's Shooter Gun Assy. (Cabinet Parts item 1, 500-5731-00) carries the launch trigger 8. ROM evidence (1.12 game start): with the ball on 16 the ROM did not fire 3 until the trigger 8 closed, then fired it once, about 0.16 s later on the host clock; the Laser Kick Test also fires 3 when 16 closes. The retained table fires a cvpmImpulseP plunger on its swPlunger trigger (script lines 1127-1143).
mechanisms.label: Auto Launch (Shooter Gun)

mechanisms.behavior: The Crane Assy. (500-5715-01, drawn at the upper left inside the arc of the left orbit with the Crane Motor 041-5027-00) carries a cab and boom on a vertical shaft turned by the motor under the playfield (schematic book printed page 76). The Crane Test text: the motor rotates in one direction only, a cam on it sweeps the crane arm through an arc of 145 degrees and back, the two limit switches 60 and 61 report the ends of the sweep, and the trigger switch pulses 'the ball release coil on the crane mechanism', the crane lock 4, whose coil assembly (515-5889-00) rides under the boom at the cab end. The cab carries two No. 89 lamps of flash drive 9. IPDB: a motorized crane target moves the ball from one ramp to another. ROM evidence (1.12 Crane Test): holding Start ran 14; the trigger 8 fired 4 once; the screen showed 'LEFT CRANE SW: ON' while 60 was held and 'RIGHT CRANE SW: ON' while 61 was held, and neither limit nor the Smart Missile button 62 fired anything. At game start, with neither limit switch ever closed, the ROM ran 14 from 5.81 s, dropped it 0.67 s after the Start press for 68 ms and ran it until 0.85 s after the ball left the shooter lane, so the run shows only that the ROM drives the motor for long stretches when no limit closes, not where it normally stops it. How a ball gets onto the boom and off it is known only from the retained table: at the right limit it enables a kicker at the end of one ramp that drops the ball into a kicker on the boom, the ball rides the boom, and its SolCraneLock kicks it off at the falling edge of 4 while the left limit 60 is closed (script lines 653-747). The table models a reversing motor that sweeps 130 degrees and waits at each end, not a cam, and whether the physical coil holds the ball while energised or releases it is not printed. No run closed a limit switch while 14 was on (in the Crane Test both limit pulses ended before Start ran the motor), so whether the ROM stops the motor at a limit is unobserved.
mechanisms.label: Crane

mechanisms.behavior: The Kick Back Assy (500-5081-00, drawn on the right wall at the upper right) on switched solenoid 22, 23-800 on the 50 V VIO-YEL supply and named 'COIL: RIPPER PIT 50V' by the ROM, kicks the ball out of the Ripper pit sensed by switch 48. IPDB: the Ripper target returns the ball at fast speed when hit. ROM evidence (1.12 Laser Kick Test, '>FEED BALL TO RIPPER<'): closing 48 fires 22 once, whether 48 is held 400 ms or 1.5 s, and closing the left outlane 43 fires nothing (the manual's Laser Kick paragraph names a left-outlane kick that reads as text shared with other Data East manuals). The retained table kicks its Sw48 kicker on 22 (script lines 593-602).
mechanisms.label: Ripper Kickback

mechanisms.behavior: The VUK Assy. (500-5690-00, drawn hatched at the top right corner) on drive 5, 23-800 through the PPB booster Q4 and named 'COIL: RIGHT VUK 50V' by the ROM, raises the ball from switch 47 onto the VUK Ramp (500-5724-00). ROM evidence (1.12 Laser Kick Test): closing 47 fires 5. The retained table kicks its bsVuk saucer on the Sw47 kicker (script lines 184-190 and 1050).
mechanisms.label: VUK (Top Right Corner)

mechanisms.behavior: The Right Scoop Ass'y on drive 6, 23-800 through the PPB booster Q3, kicks the ball out of the right scoop sensed by switch 31 (Right Scoop Assembly, 500-5057-00). ROM evidence (1.12 Laser Kick Test): closing 31 fires 6. In the retained table the right wire ramp, entered over the Right Scoop Rollover 38, ends in the scoop; that routing is the table's model.
mechanisms.label: Right Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: The middle scoop coil on drive 15 (23-800) kicks the ball out of the scoop sensed by switch 57 (Middle Scoop Left); the switch chart (printed page 29) names 58 Middle Scoop Right, the scoop's second switch. Major Assemblies item 19 (Double Scoop, 515-5772-01) is drawn above the centre between two scoop assemblies. ROM evidence (1.12 Laser Kick Test): closing 57 fires 15, while closing the Middle Scoop Right switch 58 fires nothing, so only 57 produced a transition on drive 15 there; the retained table pulses 58 from a subway switch that does not hold the ball. Four lamps 52-54 and 56 form one row of Middle Scoop inserts.
mechanisms.label: Middle Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: The Lock Ball Assy. (500-5730-00, drawn on the left side in the hatched lock area) on drive 7 (27-1400 in the coil table and on the wiring sheet, named 'COIL: LEFT LOCK' by the ROM) releases balls held in the left lock, sensed at 22 (top) and 23 (bottom). The schematic book's Ball Lock Assembly drawing of the same part number (printed page 73) shows a vertical coil (COIL, 27-1500) whose lock-ball plunger stands up out of its top bracket with a spring around it, and two actuator switches (180-5128-00, the part the switch table types for 22 and 23) beside the plunger with their arms reaching over the top. It draws no ball and does not say which way the plunger moves when the coil is energised, so whether the energised coil withdraws the plunger to release the balls is not printed. ROM evidence (1.12): in the game-start run 7 was the first solenoid the ROM switched on (7 first) once the outputs the attract and game-start lamp shows drive by themselves (9, 10, 11, 23 and 25-32) are left out, as the run's note says; the G.I. relay 11 had already switched. The Laser Kick Test fires nothing from 22 or 23. The retained table drops a post wall when 7 turns on and restores it after a timer (SolLockRelease, LockReleaseTimer, script lines 535-547).
mechanisms.label: Left Ball Lock

mechanisms.behavior: The 5 Bank Drop Target (500-5621-05) on the left side of the playfield: targets C, R, A, N and E on switches 17 (bottom) to 21 (top), as the ROM names them, reset together by drive 13 (23-800 on the operator manual's coil-driver drawing, the only drive table that prints its winding; the wiring sheet labels it 'DROP TARGET' without one), with the CRANE letter lamps 17-21. The schematic book's 5-Bank Drop Target Assembly drawing (printed page 74, part 500-5621-05, 'ADJUSTABLE') lists a '23-700 COIL' (090-5022-00), a plunger/link assembly, a target lift bracket, a target reset spring and a switch assembly (180-5092-01), and prints '*QUANTITY IS DESIGNATED BY BANK SIZE' under its table. Switch 54, the Drop Target Bar (printed '(2)', the ROM's X2), is the DANGER bar behind the bank: the manual's rule text (printed page 4) warns that 'hitting the DANGER bar behind the drop targets will reset the drop target bank', so the game, not a linkage, resets the bank through drive 13 when 54 closes. No retained page draws the bar, and no retained run closed 54 or exercised a reset in a game. The retained table pulses 54 from its sw54 target beside the bank and raises all five targets on 13 (script lines 501-511).
mechanisms.label: Five-Bank Drop Targets (CRANE)

mechanisms.behavior: The Diverter (515-5453-00, drawn on the left ramp entry) on drive 12 (27-1400). No switch reports its position, and no retained run exercised it in a game. The retained table swings its diverter open while 12 is on and back when it turns off.
mechanisms.label: Ramp Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Three Magnet Coils (090-5042-00) across the centre of the playfield on the 50 V supply. Hardware: the Magnet Control Board (520-5068-00, schematic book printed pages 70-71) takes the CPU's PIA2 port B lines PB0-PB2 from CN3 pins 9, 8 and 7 into a 74HCT273, which latches them on the clock edge from CPU CN1-7 and is cleared from CPU CN2-1; each latched output gates a P20N10 MOSFET that grounds one magnet. The schematic book does not show when the CPU clocks or clears the latch. Emulator: PinMAME models neither the clock nor the clear; once per vertical blank it publishes at 37-39 the last port B value written before the interval OR-ed with every write during it (or, on its modulated path, the PWM state), so a public level is neither the CPU's instantaneous data line nor the latched magnet state, and the physical latch timing stays unresolved. Table: the retained table approximates the board by holding each cvpmMagnet on while its public output is on; it puts 37 on the left, 38 in the centre below them and 39 on the right, and no retained page says where each magnet is. The Magnet Test 'rapidly cycles the 3 magnets ... as long as the start button is operated' and the manual warns not to run it more than a few seconds because of the high current; the 1.12 ROM turned the public addresses 38, 37 and 39 on in turn, which the board's wiring makes outputs 1, 2 and 3; those are public address transitions, not magnet timing.
mechanisms.label: Playfield Magnets

mechanisms.behavior: Three Turbo Bumper Assys (500-5227-00) in the upper right quarter, sensed at 33-35 (180-5015-01) and fired by switched solenoids 17-19 (23-800), with lamps 6-8. The third bumper sits below the left and right ones; the manual's tables call it Bottom (switch 34), Center (coil 18) and Top (lamp 7), and the ROM BOTTOM for all three. No retained run paired a bumper switch with its coil in a game; the retained table lets its VPX bumpers kick on contact.
mechanisms.label: Turbo Bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two Slingshot Assys (500-5226-00) sensed at 36 and 37 (180-5054-00) and fired by switched solenoids 20 and 21 (23-800). No retained run paired a slingshot switch with its coil in a game; the retained table lets its VPX slingshots kick on contact.
mechanisms.label: Slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Two captive-ball lanes, each with a rollover and a target: left (39, 40) and right (55, 56). Neither lane has a coil. The manual's rule text (printed page 4) says each captive-ball shot advances the M-BALL countdown by one, and that the left return lane lights the right captive ball and the right return lane the left one 'for a time period to score 2 captive ball hits'. ROM evidence (1.12, a game in play): closing the return lanes 41 and 42, the captive targets 40 and 56 and the captive rollovers 39 and 55 one at a time changed public lamp 31 in every step (4 to 17 transitions) and never changed 32. The Lamp Locations drawing prints 31 at both captive-ball inserts, while the schematic book's lamp sheet names lamps 31 and 32 Left and Right Captive Ball; that disagreement is recorded as a conflict on lamp 31.
mechanisms.label: Captive Balls

mechanisms.behavior: The Shaker Motor (515-5893-00) inside the cabinet, run by its Shaker Motor P.C. Board (520-5065-00) from drive 16. ROM evidence (1.12 game start): the ROM switched 16 on 7 times after Start, 7 times as the ball reached the release position and 6 times while it rested in the shooter lane. The retained table does not model it.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet Shaker Motor

physical.notes: Left half of the Left/Right relay pair on drive 1 (CPU transistor Q46, CN-11 pin 1, 'GRY-BRN' into PPB J1-1); the right half, the flash-lamp set, is published at 25. The coil-driver schematic draws the coil '6 Ball Ass'y Lockout 25-1240' on 'VIO-BRN (J2-10)' with power 'BRN J6-3 +32 VL'. The schematic book's wiring sheet (printed page 50) draws it as '6 BALL LOCKOUT 25-1240 1L' on the '+32VL PPB J6-2/1 BRN' bus. The retained table binds SolCallback(1) = SolTrough, which kicks the ball from its sw14 kicker into its sw15 kicker and sets switch 15 (script lines 373 and 1108-1113). The PPB-1 board schematic (printed page 67) draws this drive's left-set output from input J1-1 on J2-9, one pin below the J2-10 that the coil-driver drawing prints and the pin 10 the wiring sheet prints on its unnamed left-set connector; the board schematic draws its own J2-10 on a short line that ends unconnected. The sources agree on the drive, its public address and its coil, so the pin numbering is a wiring detail: the record follows the game's two drawings, which agree, and records no conflict. The wiring sheet takes the coil's BRN supply from '+32VL PPB J6-2/1' where the coil-driver table prints J6-3; both are 32 V, and the record keeps the table's pin. The six-ball trough's lockout: it kicks the ball at trough position 14 into the release position 15. Major Assemblies item 10 (6 Ball Switch Assy., 500-5683-01) is the trough, and item 23 (Lock Ball Assembly, 500-5684-00) is drawn beside it at the lower right. The schematic book's Trough Assembly page (printed page 75) draws Lock Ball Assembly 500-5684-01 with this drive's coil, 'COIL, 25-1240' (090-5034-00), laid horizontally beside a lock-ball link and cam, above the 6 Ball Switch Assembly and that assembly's own 23-800 coil; its suffix is -01 where the Major Assemblies list prints -00. Placed on the retained table's Kicker sw14, the table's model of the mechanism this coil actuates, not a claimed winding centre. ROM evidence (1.12 Cycling Coils): the automatic test names public 1 'COIL: LOCK OUT' and fires it as step 1 of its 29-step cycle.

Left half of the Left/Right relay pair on drive 2 (CPU transistor Q45, CN-11 pin 3, 'GRY-RED' into PPB J1-2); the right half, the flash-lamp set, is published at 26. The coil-driver schematic draws the coil 'Ball Release 23-800' on 'VIO-RED (J2-9)' with power 'BRN J6-3 +32 VL'. The schematic book's wiring sheet (printed page 50) draws it as 'BALL RELEASE 23-800 2L' on the '+32VL PPB J6-2/1 BRN' bus. The retained table binds SolCallback(2) = SolRelease, which kicks its sw15 kicker into the shooter lane and clears switch 15 (script lines 374 and 1115-1121). The PPB-1 board schematic (printed page 67) draws this drive's left-set output from input J1-2 on J2-8, one pin below the J2-9 that the coil-driver drawing prints and the pin 9 the wiring sheet prints on its unnamed left-set connector. The sources agree on the drive, its public address and its coil, so the pin numbering is a wiring detail: the record follows the game's two drawings, which agree, and records no conflict. The wiring sheet takes the coil's BRN supply from '+32VL PPB J6-2/1' where the coil-driver table prints J6-3; both are 32 V, and the record keeps the table's pin. The schematic book's Trough Assembly page (printed page 75) draws the 6 Ball Switch Assembly 500-5683-01 (Major Assemblies item 10) with this coil, 'COIL, 23-800' (090-5001-00), standing under the low end of its row of trough switches. Placed on the retained table's Kicker sw15, the table's model of the mechanism this coil actuates, not a claimed winding centre. ROM evidence (1.12 Cycling Coils): the automatic test names public 2 'COIL: BALL RELEASE' and fires it as step 3 of its 29-step cycle.

Left half of the Left/Right relay pair on drive 3 (CPU transistor Q44, CN-11 pin 4, 'GRY-ORG' into PPB J2-3); the right half, the flash-lamp set, is published at 27. The coil-driver schematic draws the coil 'Ball Launch 23-800' on 'WHT-ORG (J2-8), J8-1 Q5 TIP 36C J8-2, VIO-ORG' with power 'YEL-VIO J7-8,9 +32 VL'. The schematic book's wiring sheet (printed page 50) draws it as 'BALL LAUNCH 23-800 3L' on the '+50VDCL PPB J7-8/9 YEL/VIO' bus. The retained table binds SolCallback(3) = AutoLaunch, which fires its cvpmImpulseP plunger on the swPlunger trigger (script lines 375 and 1127-1143). The print spells the coil wire 'VIO-ORG'; it is recorded as VIO-ORN (ORN for the print's ORG). The print spells the CPU line 'GRY-ORG'; it is recorded as GRY-ORN (ORN for the print's ORG). The coil-driver drawing prints the PPB input 'J2-3' where the other six left drives print J1. The wiring sheet (printed page 50) brings all eight drive lines into one fifteen-pin PPB connector, pin 3 for this drive, and the PPB-1 board schematic (printed page 67) names that input J1-3, so the record reads the drawing's J2 as the input header J1. The PPB-1 board schematic (printed page 67) draws this drive's left-set output from input J1-3 on J2-7, one pin below the J2-8 that the coil-driver drawing prints and the pin 8 the wiring sheet prints on its unnamed left-set connector. The sources agree on the drive, its public address and its coil, so the pin numbering is a wiring detail: the record follows the game's two drawings, which agree, and records no conflict. The record follows the board's own schematic and the coil-driver drawing; the disagreement is a wiring detail, so no conflict is recorded. Both changeover contacts are drawn de-energised, their joined moving contacts resting on contacts 2 and 1, and they carry the feed from CN9 pins 1 and 3 to CN8 pins 1-4, which the board joins; contacts 4 and 3 are connected to nothing, and CN8 pins 6-9 take CN9 pins 2 and 4 straight through. The Coil/Flash Lamp sheet's General Illumination Lines draw the power-supply connector (CN8 by its nine pins and its unconnected pin 5) with pins 1-4 (BRN, YEL, GRN, VIO) as '6.3 VAC OUTPUT TO BULBS' and pins 6-9 to the PPB board's G.I. fuses F4, F3, F2 and F1 (WHT/BRN, WHT/YEL, WHT/GRN, WHT/VIO), whose fused sides return to the bulbs. The fuse drawing (operator manual printed page 2, Detail A) labels those fuses, 'All 5A S.B.', F1 'Playfield', F2 'Backbox Door & Speaker Panel', F3 'Playfield & Coin Door' and F4 'Backbox Door'. So energising 11 opens the common feed of every G.I. line, and the playfield, backbox door, speaker panel and coin door G.I. go dark together. s11.c types 11 CORE_MODOUT_BULB_44_6_3V_AC_REV for the lah_ games ('GI output', line 1225), and what a consumer reads at 11 depends on the read path. The binary solenoid state is the relay drive: 1 energises the relay and the G.I. is dark, 0 releases it and the G.I. is lit. With modulated or physical solenoid outputs enabled (CORE_MODOUT_ENABLE_MODSOL or CORE_MODOUT_ENABLE_PHYSOUT_SOLENOIDS), core_getSol(11) returns the integrated brightness of the G.I. bulbs instead (core.c line 2464): the bulb type sets isReversed (lines 3422-3429) and the bulb model applies it before integrating (line 3265), so that value is already the G.I. brightness and must not be inverted again. The schematic book's Magnet Control Board connections (520-5068-00, printed page 70) take ORG-BRN from CPU CN3-9 into J1-6 'INPUT 2' and bring 'OUTPUT 2' out on J2-4 BLU-GRY to 'MAGNET 2'. The board's schematic (printed page 71) latches the input in its 74HCT273 U1 (2D/2Q) on the CLK edge (J1-9, BRN-WHT from CPU CN1-7; CLR on J1-5, GRY-BLK from CPU CN2-1) and drives the Q2 P20N10 MOSFET through R12 39K, whose drain is J2-4; each drain has a 1N4934 diode to J2-1 '+V', which the connections sheet labels '+ 50VDC' (VIO-YEL from PPB J7-3).
